title: Falafel
subtitle: Crisp chickpea patties with herbs and spice
excerpt: Falafel are small deep-fried chickpea patties loaded with fresh herbs and warm spices. They are crisp on the outside and tender in the middle. Serve in flatbread with yoghurt, pickles, and salad.
sourceNotes: Falafel is one of the most widely eaten street foods across the Middle East, with roots in Egypt, Lebanon, and Israel. Chickpea falafel is the most common form.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked falafel on a tray, then transfer to a bag. Fry from frozen, adding 2 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch and freeze uncooked portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The mix can be made and refrigerated for up to 24 hours before shaping and frying.

content.text: Do not use canned chickpeas that have been blended smooth. The mix needs texture. Pulse the food processor in short bursts and stop when the mixture just holds together when pressed.
Drain the chickpeas well. Spread them on a clean tea towel and pat dry. Moisture makes them fall apart when frying.
Put the onion, garlic, parsley, and coriander in the food processor. Pulse until finely chopped.
Add the chickpeas, spices, and flour. Pulse in short bursts until the mix is coarse and holds together. Do not over-blend.
Season well with salt. Test by pressing a small amount together. It should hold.
Refrigerate the mix for 30 minutes. This makes shaping much easier.
Shape into balls about the size of a golf ball. Flatten slightly.
Heat the oil in the stockpot to 175C. Test with a small piece of mix. It should sizzle and float.
Fry 4 to 5 falafel at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Repeat with the rest.

items.symptom: The falafel fall apart in the oil.
items.cause: Too much moisture or the mix was over-processed.
items.fix: Add more flour and chill for 30 minutes before frying again.

items.symptom: The falafel are dark brown outside but raw inside.
items.fix: Lower heat to 170C and fry for longer on each side.
